working_title: "Did the video go up?" Four answers, four hang-ups

research_analysis.exact_observed_hook: "Hello?" (the contractor answering). Persistent on-screen text: "RED FLAGS FOR CONTRACTORS".
research_analysis.visual_hook: A man in an orange hoodie and backwards black cap sits at a desk with a laptop, a plant and a pile of $100 bills, reaching for a corded desk phone, under bold red and white text.
research_analysis.narrative_structure: 19.8 seconds, 3 cuts, 4 scenes at the same desk. In each scene he wears a different outfit, a caller on a phone-filtered voice says one red-flag sentence, and he hangs up. The hang-ups get more forceful, ending with a slam and a thrown hand.
research_analysis.viral_mechanism: A fast type-list where every entry ends with the same physical punchline. The outfit change signals 'new caller' without a word, and the hang-up lets the viewer enjoy a response they are not allowed to give in real life.
research_analysis.observed_evidence: 1.2M views on a 7.4K-follower account with a 1.8K median (660.8x). Four one-line callers in under 20 seconds. Phone ring and receiver slam sound effects. No music. Caption: "I can't be the only one that deals with this."
research_analysis.performance_hypothesis: Hypothesis: the caption invites people in the same trade to confirm it happens to them, and each line is short enough to quote in a comment. At 20 seconds with four payoffs, completion is high.
research_analysis.why_this_format_fits_alex: It is the '2 Types of Clients' idea (client behaviour, acted, at a desk) compressed to 20 seconds with four characters. The repeated physical action reads without sound.
research_analysis.originality_changes: Borrowed: same desk, outfit per caller, one line each on a filtered voice, a physical sign-off every time. New: it is one repeated question from Alex after delivering a video, the four answers are new, the action is placing the phone face down, and the last beat changes the action (phone goes in a drawer, the drawer buzzes).

alex_adaptation.concept: Alex has delivered the video. He calls to ask one thing: did it go up? Four clients give four reasons it has not been posted. Each time he calmly sets the phone face down. The fourth time the phone goes in a drawer.
alex_adaptation.target_audience: Agency owners, freelancers, social media managers. Also business owners sitting on unposted content.
alex_adaptation.first_frame: Alex at the desk, phone to his ear, hopeful face, mid-question. Bold text at top: "ME: 'DID THE VIDEO GO UP?'"
alex_adaptation.first_spoken_line: Hey! Just checking, did the video go up?

full_script.speaker: Alex
full_script.dialogue: Hey! Just checking, did the video go up?
full_script.action: Bright, hopeful, leaning in. Grey tee.
full_script.camera: Static, chest-up at the desk, locked tripod.
full_script.editing: Top text stays all video. Captions for client lines only, in yellow.

full_script.speaker: Client 1 (Alex's voice, phone filter)
full_script.dialogue: Not yet. We're waiting for the right moment.
full_script.action: Alex listens. Smile fades to neutral. He takes the phone from his ear, looks at it, and sets it face down on the desk with two fingers.
full_script.editing: Jump cut at 6s on the phone touching the desk.
full_script.audio: Phone-filtered voice. Soft 'tap' as the phone lands.

full_script.speaker: Client 2
full_script.dialogue: So my mom watched it, and she says my voice sounds weird.
full_script.action: New outfit: hoodie. Phone already at his ear. Eyes close for a full second on 'my mom'. Phone face down, a little firmer.

full_script.speaker: Client 3
full_script.dialogue: We actually want to grow our followers first. Then we'll start posting.
full_script.action: New outfit: button-up. He hears it, blinks twice, mouths 'grow first' to himself, looks at the camera for half a second. Phone face down, firm.

full_script.speaker: Client 4
full_script.dialogue: Oh, we posted it! Yeah. To Close Friends.
full_script.action: New outfit: jacket. Alex nods slowly. He opens the desk drawer, places the phone inside, closes the drawer, folds his hands on the desk and looks ahead.
full_script.editing: No cut. Let the drawer action play in real time.

full_script.speaker: None
full_script.action: The drawer buzzes. Alex does not move. Only his eyes go down to the drawer, then back up.
full_script.on_screen_text: Small text near the drawer: "quick thought"
full_script.editing: Cut on his eyes returning forward.
full_script.audio: Phone vibration inside the drawer, two pulses.

alternate_hooks: Top text: "REASONS THE VIDEO ISN'T POSTED YET"
Top text: "I'm 23 and my whole job is getting brands to press 'post'"
Open on client 4's line ("We posted it! To Close Friends.") with the drawer, then text "Earlier that week" and run the other three
alternate_endings: Fifth caller: "We posted it and it got a million views." Alex freezes, then very carefully sets the phone down face up and backs away from it.
After the drawer closes, Alex pulls out a second phone, dials, and says "Hey! Just checking, did the video go up?" (loops)
alex_adaptation.caption: The video is done. It has been done. #agencylife

production.wardrobe: Four tops kept within reach: grey tee, hoodie, button-up, jacket
shot_list: Outfit 1: opening question plus client 1 reaction and phone down
Outfit 2: client 2 reaction and phone down
Outfit 3: client 3 reaction, look to camera, phone down
Outfit 4: client 4 reaction, drawer, buzz, eyes
Audio-only: four client lines in four slightly different voices
production.editor_instructions: Lock the tripod so only the outfit changes between cuts. Start each new scene with the phone already at his ear to save time. Phone-filter all four client lines and pitch each one slightly differently. Raise the volume of each phone 'tap' a little more than the last. Add a real phone-vibration sound for the drawer. No music.

variants_to_test: Alternate hook: top text 'REASONS THE VIDEO ISN'T POSTED YET'
Alternate payoff: the client whose video hit a million views
testing.promotion_decision: Brand fit 3. Promote at 48h if views are at least 3x the trailing median and shares per 1,000 reached are top quartile; if follows per 1,000 is 2x median at low views, re-film with the age-and-job top text.
follow_up_variations_if_successful: Same desk: four responses to 'can you film on Thursday?'
Same desk: four responses to the first invoice
Same desk: four different clients reacting to their first viral video, each one worse at handling it

creative_confidence.rationale: Twenty seconds, four payoffs, one desk, and the phone-down action reads with the sound off. 'Grow our followers first, then post' is the line most likely to be quoted.
uncertainties: Client lines are comedic composites and must not be captioned as real quotes from named clients
The reference used escalating slams; a quiet phone-down is subtler and relies on Alex's face
Top text carries the setup, so the first frame must hold it long enough to read
